tasks.instruction:
Make nested glom specifications behave consistently wherever an operator accepts a child specification. Child specs must be evaluated against the current target and scope, including when they are nested inside Spec wrappers or other composite specifications, rather than being returned as literal values. Preserve an explicit way to request literal values, and do not reinterpret structural arguments such as path strings, mapping keys, match predicates, or switch case labels as specs.

This behavior must cover recursive Spec composition, Match fallbacks, Switch selectors/cases/fallbacks, Assign values, subspecs embedded in T expressions, and values assigned through S scope variables. Match and Switch defaults must be evaluated as child specs when supplied, while omitting a default must retain their normal no-match behavior. Assign must evaluate a spec-valued assignment before storing it, and S assignments must evaluate their right-hand side in the current scope so later specifications can read the assigned variable. The same rules must hold through multiple levels of nesting and for combinations with dot-delimited paths, callable invocations, T expressions, and other existing glom features.

The completed behavior is observable through the existing tests named “spec and recursion”, “match default”, “switch”, “assign spec val”, “t subspec”, and “s scope assign”: each must pass without special-casing only one nesting depth or one operator, and existing literal-value and error behavior must remain compatible.
tasks.title: Unify nested spec evaluation across glom operators

tasks.instruction:
Ensure glom.core can consistently evaluate and report callable-based specifications on all supported Python versions, including built-in functions, ordinary functions, bound methods, partials, and callable objects. Callable invocation must correctly resolve positional and keyword arguments from glom specifications, preserve the expected target and scope behavior, and support zero-argument and multi-argument callables.

The completed behavior must support the existing invoke, check, test, assign, path/T round-trip, flatten, fold, sum, and filter workflows. Checks and predicates must return their documented values, apply defaults or raise the documented glom errors when validation fails, and retain useful formatted context identifying the failing operation and path. Assignments must create or update nested destinations addressed by dot-delimited paths without corrupting existing data. Path conversion to and from T expressions must preserve equivalent paths, including paths that require non-attribute access. Flattening, folding, summing integer values, and filtering must work when their callable arguments are built-ins as well as user-defined callables.

Do not make behavior depend on callable repr formats or introspection APIs that differ between Python implementations or versions. Existing public APIs and normal error types must remain compatible, and invalid paths, failed predicates, unsupported argument shapes, and callable exceptions must produce the library’s established error behavior rather than being silently ignored.
tasks.title: Make callable-based glom specs reliable across platforms
